Elena (PM): Heads-up — FinCorp just signed the private deployment LOI. They need low-latency, single-tenant inference with HSM-backed keys and strict network isolation. We need a cross-team sequencing plan by EOD Friday.
Marcus (Eng): Got it. Rough ask: dedicated GPU pool, pinned model versions, and SLA 99.9. Any perf targets from the customer?
Elena (PM): FinCorp wants p95 < 120ms for common prompts, and token cost within 1.5x our hosted baseline. Also must support audit logs and retention settings.
Priya (Runtime): p95 <120ms depends on model size and quantization. Which models are they expecting?
Elena (PM): They're prototyping on a 13B open model (decoder-only). They asked for two variants: fp16 and int4-ish quantized for cost.
Sam (Infra): We'll need a dedicated VPC subnet + egress rules, and capacity planning for prewarm + burst. How many concurrent users?
Leo (Solutions): FinCorp expects bursts of ~200 concurrent chat sessions during business hours, steady 30 concurrent otherwise. Sessions average 60 tokens per response.
Marcus (Eng): 200 concurrent for 13B with p95 <120ms is doable with reserved instances and batching config, but requires runtime KV cache warmup and prewarmed workers. Need autoscale policy too.
Dana (Security): HSM/KMS integration is required. We need a list of keys to manage and whether customer brings own key (BYOK). Also SOC/PCI questions — will data persist?
Elena (PM): They will BYOK and want seven-day raw log retention within their VPC only. No PII retention beyond traces.
Priya (Runtime): For BYOK plus private control plane we need a secure tunnel to their KMS endpoint or customer-hosted HSM. That affects our rollout order: security plumbing must land before runtime can enable key-wrapped caching.
Jordan (Release): Can we sketch a gated rollout timeline? I propose
- Week 0: infra + security basics (network + KMS connection)
- Week 1: runtime private deploy + quantization tests
- Week 2: end-to-end e2e + perf canary + compliance review
- Week 3: pilot with 5% traffic then ramp
Marcus (Eng): Sounds reasonable. Question: quantization tests — who owns building/loading the int4 kernels and validating quality regressions? Priya/Eng-ML?
Priya (Runtime): Runtime owns integration and perf validation. Eng-ML should own quality checks and prompt-set evals. Can we get a prompt set from FinCorp?
Elena (PM): I'll request a 100-case prompt set and a pass/fail criteria doc.
Dana (Security): Compliance review needs audit logs, key access logs, and attestations. We need to run a baseline pen-test for the private control plane before pilot.
Sam (Infra): Also need capacity for staging that mirrors production traffic patterns. Prefer infra to provision a mirror pool for canary.
Leo (Solutions): I'll coordinate with FinCorp on a test harness and synthetic replay. That'll help runtime simulate the session mix.
Marcus (Eng): Operational concerns: fallback when quantized model diverges beyond threshold. Suggest policy: if quality drop > 3% on eval set, auto-fallback to fp16 variant and alert. Who implements the fallback logic? (runtime + platform)
Priya (Runtime): Runtime will implement fallback hooks and roll policy. We need a config flag per-tenant: preferred_variant -> [int4, fp16] and auto-fallback thresholds.
Jordan (Release): Rollout gating checklist (quick):
```
- infra: VPC + subnet + firewall rules configured
- security: BYOK integration tested, key access logs enabled
- runtime: model variant + quantization validated, KV cache policy set
- perf: p95 <120ms on canary for 30m window
- quality: eval pass rate >= 97% on FinCorp prompt set
- observability: per-tenant dashboards + cost breakdown present
- rollback: automated fallback and circuit-breaker enabled
```
Elena (PM): Great. Let's assign owners: Sam -> infra items, Dana -> security + pen-test, Priya -> runtime integration + fallback, Marcus -> autoscale config + capacity, Leo -> test harness + prompt set, Jordan -> gates checklist + release windows. I'll own product acceptance and customer comms.
Sam (Infra): I'll provision staging pool and ensure network policies. ETA: Wed EOD.
Dana (Security): Pen-test scheduling request: can we get a windows next Thursday? I need at least 48h notice.
Leo (Solutions): I'll ask FinCorp for the prompt set today and mock traffic generator by Tue.
Marcus (Eng): Autoscale policy draft: keep 10 prewarmed workers, scale based on concurrent_sessions, scale step 20 workers per burst, cooldown 30s. Posting draft in #eng-runtime.
Priya (Runtime): Noted. For quant kernels we need a microbenchmark run: `run_quant_bench --model 13B --batch 1 --seq 128` — I'll run this on the staging pool after infra is up.
Elena (PM): OK everyone — action items and owners recorded. Quick ask: can each owner update the doc in Confluence by EOD Thursday? Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/fin-private-deploy (will add the prompt set when received).
Marcus (Eng): I'll update autoscale + cost estimates.
Jordan (Release): I'll lock tentative pilot window: start two weeks from next Monday, pending pass gates.
deploy-bot: Build started for branch `fincorp/private-onramp` (CI #4521)
Dana (Security): Running a quick checklist now — will add required attestations to the Confluence page.
Elena (PM): Thanks all. If anything blocks, ping me or drop in #product. :pray:
Marcus (Eng): One more: we should define SLO error budget for the SSD-backed KV cache fallback. I'll draft proposed SLOs and post inline.
Priya (Runtime): Cool — meet tomorrow 10am to align on perf test harness and metrics.
Elena (PM): Meeting confirmed 10am tomorrow. End of thread.
